newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ Osaka chief disappointed by reaction to tankan.
newsitem.headline: BOJ Osaka chief disappointed by reaction to tankan.

text.p: The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) Osaka branch manager Eiichiro Kinoshita told a news conference on Friday that he was disappointed by the reaction of financial markets to the BOJ's "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment.

"I felt that the tankan results were pretty good this time. Business sentiment improved and sales and profits were higher than expected. Capital investments have been revised upwards, too, which is a strong factor," Kinoshita said.
"Looking at the overall situation, I am disappointed and feel awkward about the market's reaction," he said.
The quarterly tankan survey, released on Wednesday, showed that the business outlook among major manufacturers had improved since the previous survey in August.
The diffusion index for big manufacturers -- an important gauge of corporate sentiment -- rose to minus three in November from minus seven in August, when the previous survey was conducted.
The tankan is regarded by financial markets as a key clue to Japan's monetary policy.
Kinoshita said the markets took the survey as indicating that the economy, which has been on a gradual recovery path, was worse than expected.

He said he hoped that private-sector demand would strengthen further in the coming months. He said he was slightly concerned with the lower profit outlook for the latter half of this fiscal year, ending next March 31.

Kinoshita said he had heard that although sales were growing, this had not contributed to growth in profits as prices of goods had not risen. On the other hand, much economic data this past month had been positive, such as a rebound in industrial production, he said.
